reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses Mn-based redox buffering and general HEA corrosion mechanisms in molten salts, but provides no specific support for the premises about Q235 steel's native oxide film, its room-temperature protectiveness, or the thermal-stress-driven breakdown mechanism proposed.
premises: Q235 steel has a native thin iron-oxide passive film at room temperature
This oxide film provides some protection at room temperature
At high temperature in molten salt, the oxide scale has poor thermodynamic stability and adherence
Accelerated diffusion and thermal stress at high temperature compromise oxide integrity
Breakdown of the oxide scale leads to rapid corrosion
